description: Oscillator producing sine, triangle, sawtooth and square waves at once, each on its own output

params.text: Switches sync from hard to soft, so a sync signal reverses the direction of the wave instead of restarting it
Sets the pitch over a range of nine octaves, giving C4 at 261.63Hz in the middle of its travel
Scales the FM input from -100% to 100%, so the modulation can be made shallow or reversed
Sets the width of the square wave's high portion, 50% in the middle of its travel; narrower and wider settings thin the sound
Scales the PWM input from -100% to 100%, so the modulation can be made shallow or reversed
Switches frequency modulation from exponential to linear, which keeps the tuning steady under audio-rate modulation

inputs.text: Pitch at a volt per octave, added to the frequency knob; the channels patched here set the oscillator's polyphony
Adds to the frequency by an amount set by the FM knob; at 100% each volt doubles the frequency
A rising edge through 0V restarts the phase of every wave, which is hard sync
Moves the width of the square wave by an amount set by the PWM knob

outputs.text: The sine wave, a single frequency with no harmonics above it
The triangle wave, with odd harmonics that fall away quickly
The sawtooth wave, with every harmonic of the fundamental present
The square wave, with odd harmonics only at a 50% width, and none of the harmonics of a saw
